purpose: Ledgerline PR1: the foundations and correctness core of a governed AI data analyst. A person asks a business question in plain English; the model will only fill in a typed intent, and plain Python checks every field against a registry before a query builder writes parameterized, read-only SQL. This PR delivers everything except the model pipeline: the project scaffold, a seeded demo database, the model gateway with replay and a budget guard, a pre-registered evaluation set, the registry and `registry init`, the intent model, the validator, the SQL builder and the read-only executor.
mechanism:
1. `ledgerline seed` (ledgerline/fieldservice/seed.py, schema.py) builds the synthetic fieldservice Postgres database from a fixed seed and sets up roles: an owner, and `ledgerline_ro`, which can only SELECT and cannot read users.email or users.password_hash (column-level REVOKE, also applied by infra/postgres/roles.sql inside one transaction).
2. The registry (ledgerline/core/registry.py) is a YAML file describing entities, fields (type, description, aliases, filterable, aggregatable, hidden, categorical), relationships and allowed values. `ledgerline registry init <db-url>` (registry_init.py) reads a database with SQLAlchemy's inspector and drafts that YAML: it infers relationships from `<x>_id` columns when no foreign key is declared (never on columns whose declared key was skipped), auto-hides sensitive-looking fields, detects categoricals, marks the file draft, and is deterministic.
3. The intent (intent.py) is the only thing a model will produce: intent type, base entity, select, metrics, filters (incl. any_of groups and column-to-column comparisons), having, group_by with calendar grains, a date range with relative tokens resolved by code (dates.py) against a fixed reference time, order_by and limit.
4. The validator (validate.py) checks an intent against the registry and returns typed errors (e.g. unknown_field, hidden_field, fan_out, ambiguous_path, ambiguous_value, having_type, alias_collision). Every rule has a named test.
5. The SQL builder (sqlbuild.py) turns a valid intent into SQLAlchemy Core: identifiers only from the registry, every value a typed bound parameter (64-bit integers, NUMERIC thresholds), joins only along many-to-one relationships (LEFT JOIN when a join is reached only through an OR group), per-dialect calendar grains, and canonical datetime text on SQLite.
6. The executor (executor.py) runs the query read-only: Postgres with BEGIN READ ONLY and statement_timeout, SQLite in mode=ro with a progress-handler timeout, a row cap, and an audit row in ask_log (audit.py) for every run, including connection failures.
7. The model gateway (ledgerline/llm/) wraps OpenRouter through LangChain with structured output, a replay store (record | replay | live), a cost meter (pricing.py) and a budget guard (budget.py) that pre-checks worst-case cost by UTF-8 bytes, aborts at the cap and resumes from a checkpoint. `ledgerline spike` checks schema compliance on candidate models (pending: no key).
8. evals/gold/ holds the pre-registered fieldservice gold set (manifest-hashed, changelog required for changes) and Spider question IDs (scripts/fetch_benchmarks.py downloads Spider with a pinned checksum; no Spider data is committed).
9. verify.sh runs ruff, pyright (strict on ledgerline/core), pytest with zero skips, per-module branch coverage (scripts/check_coverage.py), detect-secrets and the privacy scan.
decisions:
- The model writes a typed intent, never SQL: no invented columns or injected values; the cost is that only what the intent can express gets answered (ADR-001).
- Correctness code (validator, builder, executor) is plain, fully tested Python; LangGraph is only used for orchestration in a later PR (ADR-002).
- Joins go only many-to-one; aggregating across a one-to-many edge is rejected (fan_out) rather than risking double counts (ADR-003).
- Ambiguous join paths are refused, not guessed; this costs coverage on schemas with two keys to the same table.
- Hidden fields are enforced twice: by the registry and by the database role.
- Replay plus a hard budget guard so tests and CI never call a live model (ADR-005).
- The gold set and Spider selection were committed before the intent model existed, so the eval is not fitted to the grammar (ADR-006).
- Rejected: letting the model write SQL directly; trusting declared foreign keys only; rounding numbers for comparison.
readers: README.md and evals/gold/README.md → people trying or evaluating the project (recruiters, developers who clone it); docs/adr/ → engineers who want the reasoning; code comments and docstrings → the next maintainer. Cristian's rule for all of them: every comment, description and doc line deliberate, plain short sentences, terms defined on first use, no jargon-heavy decision prose.
